_note: The SHARED lint rule FACTS (doc 09 'Linter strategy — one rule source, two runners', step 1): the ground-truth tables both runners load — ClosedSource/scripts/lint_dsx.rb (the authoritative repo gate, unchanged rules) and the TS linter (OpenSource/Web/packages/compiler/src/lint.ts, the dev-loop twin). Rule FACTS live here so they cannot drift; rule LOGIC lives in each runner and is anti-drifted by the fixture corpus beside this file (cases/ + expected diagnostics, both runners in CI). Editing a table here changes BOTH linters at once — run both gates.
_valuelessInputTagsNote: Text inputs whose factories read `bind=` and never look at `value=`, on every renderer. `value=` is the spelling for what a <text>, <image> or <progress> SHOWS, so an author reaches for it here by analogy and gets a field that renders empty: no error, no warning, nothing bound. `progress` is deliberately NOT in this set - it reads `bind ?? value`. Verified factory by factory (dom/src/elements.ts `textfield`, which `searchbar` aliases, and `textareaEl`).
_bareExpressionAttrsNote: Attributes the renderers read through bindValue: the RAW attribute string is evaluated as one JSE expression, so a {{ }} wrapper is a dict literal rather than the value. visible-if then never hides, and a data attribute like commands= silently resolves to nothing at all - the surface renders empty and reports no error.
headOrderHint: attribute → override → expects → event/input/tool → api/variable (plain → computed) → formula → action → script → watch → style → component
_harnessAttrsNote: Attributes the MOUNT CONTRACT consumes on any element (layout words, row/binding words, icon/tooltip affordances) - allowed everywhere by the R9 attribute-vocabulary rule even where an element's own census does not list them. A word here is a harness seam, not an element attribute.
_cssHabitAttrsNote: CSS property names written as ATTRIBUTES - the habit every ex-web author and every AI brings. Each maps to real style-plane vocabulary (dsx-css-properties.json), so the linters answer with the style= spelling instead of a census notice; the kebab-case spelling of any mapped property (margin-top=) is the same habit and gets the same error. Names that ARE element vocabulary (gap, position, inset, display) must stay out of this table; the runners skip any entry the census already admits. cssHabitPxProps names the properties whose bare-number example value gets a px suffix in the message.
